issues.t: Automatic transmission slips or shifts harshly
issues.sym: Slipping once the car is warm, a missing gear, delayed or jerky shifts, or a lurch when shifting into gear.
issues.why: The 200SX shares its 4-speed automatic with the Sentra of the same years, and owners of these cars report slipping and failures as they age. Old fluid and overheating speed up wear.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and condition. If it slips or will not engage, stop driving it hard and get a transmission diagnosis; a used or rebuilt unit is the usual fix.

issues.t: Check engine light with transmission codes but no shifting problem
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on with codes such as P0731, P0732 or P0733 (or P0120 or P0510), yet the car drives and shifts normally.
issues.why: Nissan issued bulletins explaining that these codes can set on these cars without any real drivability fault, often from sensor signals or adjustments rather than a failing transmission.
issues.next: Have the codes read and ask the shop to check the Nissan bulletins before replacing transmission parts.

issues.t: Timing chain rattle and front cover leaks
issues.sym: A rattle from the front of the engine, often worse at start-up, and sometimes oil seeping from the timing cover.
issues.why: The 1.6L engine uses a timing chain with a spring-loaded tensioner and guides that wear. Nissan revised its service procedure for the front cover and timing chain on this engine, and owners report badly worn sprockets.
issues.next: Have a rattling timing chain checked soon. A worn chain can skip a tooth and cause serious engine damage.

issues.t: Misfire or rough running from spark plug wires
issues.sym: Rough idle, shaking, hesitation on acceleration, and a check engine light that may flash.
issues.why: Nissan found that spark plug wires on some of these cars break down and leak spark, causing misfires.
issues.next: Have the plug wires and plugs checked. If the check engine light flashes, pull over when it's safe and turn the engine off.

issues.t: Check engine light for random misfire code P0300
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on with code P0300, sometimes with a slight stumble.
issues.why: Nissan issued a bulletin for P0300 misfire codes on cars within certain VIN ranges.
issues.next: Have the codes read and the ignition parts checked. Ask whether the bulletin applies to your VIN.

issues.t: Unstable idle and code P0505 from the idle air valve
issues.sym: Idle speed that hunts up and down, stalls at stops, or a check engine light with code P0505.
issues.why: The idle air control valve can stick or fail. Nissan also found some cars with the valve's power wiring reversed.
issues.next: Have the valve and wiring tested. Cleaning helps in some cases; a failed valve is replaced.

issues.t: Check engine light for airflow sensor code P0100
issues.sym: The check engine light is on with code P0100. The car may hesitate or run poorly.
issues.why: Nissan issued a bulletin about the mass airflow sensor code being stored on these cars.
issues.next: Have the sensor and its connector checked before replacing parts.

issues.t: Check engine light for rear oxygen sensor or catalyst codes
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on with code P0137 or P0420, often with no change in how the car drives.
issues.why: Nissan issued bulletins on the rear oxygen sensor and catalyst checks for these cars.
issues.next: Have the codes read. You can usually keep driving, but you may fail an emissions test until it is fixed.

issues.t: Wipers can stop working (recall)
issues.sym: The wipers slow down, stop part way, or stop moving altogether, often in heavy rain.
issues.why: Water gets into a ball joint in the wiper linkage, washes out the grease, and the joint wears until the linkage comes apart from the motor.
issues.next: Do not drive in rain or snow without working wipers. Ask a Nissan dealer to check this recall with your VIN.

issues.t: A/C high-pressure hose leaks (service campaign)
issues.sym: The A/C blows warm air or cools poorly, sometimes after slowly losing refrigerant.
issues.why: Nissan ran a service campaign to replace the A/C high-pressure hose on Sentra and 200SX models. The campaign is no longer active.
issues.next: Have the A/C checked for leaks before recharging it, and inspect the high-pressure hose.

issues.t: Horn sounds on its own
issues.sym: The horn honks by itself while driving or parked.
issues.why: Nissan issued a bulletin on random horn operation for cars in certain VIN ranges.
issues.next: Have the horn switch and wiring in the steering wheel checked. Pulling the horn fuse stops it temporarily, but you need a working horn.

issues.t: Seat belt latch can slide down the belt
issues.sym: The metal tongue on the front seat belt slides down to the floor when the belt is not in use, so it is hard to reach.
issues.why: The small button that keeps the latch plate in place on the belt can be missing. Nissan issued several bulletins on it.
issues.next: Have the button replaced so the belt is easy to use. Make sure the belt still buckles and retracts properly.

issues.t: Airbag light on or airbags not working as expected
issues.sym: The airbag warning light blinks or stays on. Owners of these years have also reported airbags that did not deploy in a crash or went off at very low speed.
issues.why: The 200SX shares its airbag system with the Sentra of the same years, which has many owner complaints about frontal airbags and their sensors.
issues.next: If the airbag light is on, have the system scanned right away. The airbags may not work in a crash while the light is on.

issues.t: Worn engine mounts (service campaign)
issues.sym: A clunk when shifting into gear or accelerating, or extra vibration at idle.
issues.why: Nissan ran a voluntary service campaign to replace engine mounts on some 1998 models.
issues.next: Ask a Nissan dealer whether the campaign was done on your car, and have the mounts inspected.

issues.t: Shift lock release button sticks or breaks
issues.sym: The automatic shifter is hard to move out of Park, or the release button is broken or sticks.
issues.why: Nissan issued a bulletin to replace the shift release button on these cars.
issues.next: Have the shifter repaired. Do not force the lever; a broken shift lock can leave you stuck in Park.

issues.t: Throttle position sensor out of adjustment
issues.sym: Uneven idle, poor shifting from the automatic, or a check engine light, sometimes with code P0510 or P0120.
issues.why: The throttle position sensor must be set precisely. Nissan revised the adjustment procedure and added a special test connector.
issues.next: Have the sensor checked and adjusted with the correct procedure before replacing it.

issues.t: Dash and tail lights go dark
issues.sym: The gauge lights black out at night, and some owners also lose the tail or side marker lights.
issues.why: The dash dimmer switch commonly fails. Owners also report lighting circuit faults that fuses and a new headlight switch did not fix.
issues.next: Driving at night without tail lights is unsafe. Check the fuses, then have the dimmer switch and lighting circuit tested.

issues.t: Torn CV axle boots
issues.sym: Grease splattered inside the wheel well, then a clicking noise when turning sharply.
issues.why: The rubber boots on the front drive axles crack and tear, letting grease out and dirt in. Owners report replacing them often.
issues.next: Replace a torn boot early. Once the joint clicks, the whole axle usually needs replacing.

issues.t: Worn front ball joints
issues.sym: Clunking from the front over bumps, loose steering, or uneven tire wear.
issues.why: The front lower ball joints wear out, and on these cars the joint is replaced together with the control arm.
issues.next: Have the front end inspected if you hear clunks. A badly worn ball joint can separate and cause a loss of control.

issues.t: Water pump leaks coolant
issues.sym: Coolant drips from the front of the engine, the coolant level drops, or the temperature gauge climbs.
issues.why: The water pump seal and gasket wear out with age.
issues.next: Do not keep driving if the engine overheats. Have the pump replaced and the cooling system refilled properly.

issues.t: Alternator fails
issues.sym: The battery light comes on, the lights dim, or the car dies and will not restart.
issues.why: Owners of these cars commonly report alternator failures.
issues.next: Have the charging system tested before replacing the battery.

issues.t: Radiator cooling fan stops working
issues.sym: The temperature climbs in traffic or with the A/C on, but is fine on the highway.
issues.why: Owners say the electric cooling fans often fail somewhere around 50,000 to 75,000 miles.
issues.next: Watch the temperature gauge. If it climbs at idle, have the fan, relay and fuse tested before the engine overheats.

issues.t: Oil leaks from the front and rear seals
issues.sym: Oil spots under the car, a burning oil smell, or oil coating the underside.
issues.why: Engine seals and the oil pan gasket harden and leak with age. Owners report losing as much as a quart every 100 miles.
issues.next: Check the oil level often and have the leak traced. A bad leak can starve the engine of oil.
